note: Description taken from Sands' 1965 revision (in English), including the alate and soldier; the worker is not treated separately; the original description is Sjöstedt 1902 (Nyasaland, Zomba) and this entry follows Sands' redescription and measurements. The OCR misread decimal points as hyphens or colons (e.g. I-16 for 1.16, 0:35 for 0.35), restored here by magnitude; where a mean is illegible only the range is cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very close to N. arborum: in this species the frons often has a shallow forked groove in front of the frontal marks (not always distinct) and the female cerci are as long as their basal width; the soldier nasus is usually more slender with more bristles at the tip, and the vertex sometimes bears bristles; it differs from N. fulleri in the 13-segmented soldier antennae (12 in fulleri) and in the alate having relatively longer hind tibiae and ocelli further from the eyes. The soldier shows size variation (different instars), which may be regarded as residual dimorphism.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut-brown, postclypeus and antennae yellowish brown, labrum pale yellowish brown; pronotum and abdominal tergites chestnut-brown, meso- and metanota brown; sides of the sternites pale brown, a narrow median strip yellowish brown; legs pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule behind the eyes nearly semicircular, only slightly wavy behind the eyes; frontal marks distinct, paler than the head capsule, Y-shaped; compound eyes short oval, moderately prominent relative to their own diameter, not large relative to head width, eye width index 3.0—3.5; ocelli small, slightly less than their own least diameter from the compound eyes; postclypeus moderately inflated, 2.8—3.0 times as wide as long, anterior margin slightly concave or wavy, posterior margin convex and rounded, distinctly wavy near the outer corners; antennae 15-segmented, II longer than III and IV (the latter two about equal) and slightly longer than V. Female cerci as long as the basal width, slightly irregularly conical. Measurements (11 specimens, 4 localities, mm): head width (across the eyes) 1.20—1.38 (mean 1.31); greatest diameter of the compound eye 0.37—0.44 (mean 0.41); ocellus 0.10—0.11 × 0.14—0.17 (mean 0.11 × 0.15); ocellus to eye 0.07—0.10 (mean 0.08); pronotum width 1.00—1.13 (mean 1.08); pronotum length 0.58—0.72 (mean 0.68); hind tibia length 1.54—1.73 (mean 1.63); fore wing length 11.60—11.90.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellow to ferruginous orange, nasus orange to ferruginous; pronotum and antennae yellow to orange-yellow; abdominal tergites and legs yellow, sternites pale yellow. Head capsule short oval in frontal view, narrowing anteriorly, nasus weakly conical; in lateral view nearly straight, sometimes slightly concave or wavy with a weak elevation at the base of the nasus; nasus shorter than the rest of the head capsule measured from the posterior margin of the antennal bases, nasus cone angle 12—15 degrees; postmental plate weakly convex; antennae 12—14-segmented, usually 13-segmented, II and IV about equal and shorter than V, III longer than V. Cephalic bristles confined to the 4 at the tip of the nasus and shorter bristles behind them, sometimes 1 pair on the vertex, plus several on the anterior margin of the postmental plate. Abdominal tergites with scattered minute fine bristles, some or all segments with a few fine short bristles at the posterior margin; sternite bristles scattered, longer at the posterior margin. Measurements (22 specimens, 16 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.33—1.70 (mean 1.53); head width 0.63—1.05 (mean 0.89); head capsule depth 0.50—0.68 (mean 0.60); pronotum width 0.42—0.64 (mean 0.48); pronotum length 0.17—0.30 (mean 0.21); hind tibia length 0.97—1.33 (mean 1.08).
